correctness.rationale: The statement is proved for every fixed 0<b<a, a+b<1, 0<epsilon<(1-a-b)/2, and t>=0. Operator-norm and PPT arguments establish full-rank separability; no numerical enumeration is used for these quantifiers. The discord reduction follows by orthogonal measurement projection, and both Gram matrices are computed exactly. The positive offdiagonal entries rule out every finite-time eigenvalue crossing when epsilon>0. Differentiable compact-uniform Taylor expansions of the exact 2x2 spectral gaps give the epsilon^2 and epsilon windows with common slope curve. The actual embedded verifier reconstructs the matrices independently (42 tested states), checks PPT invariance, formula equality and scaled slopes, and passed. Finite checks only corroborate the analytic proof.

originality.rationale: Published precursor results give the two-qubit geometric-discord spectral formula, sudden-change eigenvalue criterion, Bell-diagonal dephasing patterns and an entropic-discord demonstration of non-ideal preparation. None of the materially inspected main results or their actual worked examples gives the paired equal-distance preparation-error families with quantitatively different epsilon^2 versus epsilon smoothing widths and identical normalized slope profile. The full text of one relevant non-X decoherence source could not be obtained and remains a documented priority risk; there is no independent confirmation of novelty.
residual_risks: The complete Chen–Fu–Fang paper could not be inspected because both OA/preprint search and an authorized institutional-download request yielded no accessible full text; the abstract concerns different Bloch-vector orientations but does not conclusively rule out equivalent asymptotic results.
A general spectral perturbation theorem might contain the same two-scale law in equivalent parameters outside the primary sources searched. No search result or partition proves global originality.
Hilbert–Schmidt geometric discord differs from entropy-based discord; claims about one cannot be transferred to the other.

value.rationale: Physical preparation errors of the same Hilbert–Schmidt size may be local Bloch offsets or bipartite cross-correlations. Their two-to-one crossover exponents, universal normalized profile, and exact recentering quantify how an idealized sharp quantum-correlation transition disappears under realistic imperfection. The result gives structurally distinct and physically motivated robustness predictions for full-rank separable states, rather than merely renaming the original Bell-diagonal formula or recomputing a known table. It is deliberately limited to explicit natural error mechanisms, not a blanket perturbation classification.
